title: C# built-in type aliases and characteristics
concepts: C# keywords alias named types in the .NET type system
Value types store values while reference types store object references
Numeric types differ in range, precision, representation, and platform dependence
The language's built-in type set includes numeric, Boolean, character, object, string, dynamic, and void forms
Choosing a type means balancing domain meaning, range, precision, interoperability, and API expectations

items: Native-sized integer aliases nint and nuint became language keywords with built-in operators and conversions

Arrays, tuples, enums, structs, classes, interfaces, and delegates

accuracyFacts: Value-type variables contain values; do not claim the language requires local value data to be stored on the stack or directly inside a physical variable slot. Object references are not specified as physical memory addresses.

decimal uses a finite-precision base-10 representation. It represents many decimal fractions exactly, but arithmetic can still round; do not claim decimal eliminates rounding errors or is always slower/faster.
char is a 16-bit UTF-16 code unit, not necessarily one complete Unicode scalar value; supplementary scalars use surrogate pairs.
Integral literal assignment outside the target type's permitted constant range is generally a compile-time error; distinguish compile-time constant conversions from runtime checked/unchecked casts.
